Function composition
Composing JavaScript functions with compose (right to left) and pipe (left to right), and writing pipe for any number of functions: loop, reduce, recursion.
Understand what function composition is and learn to chain functions with compose and pipe, both for three functions and for any number of them.
text
Function composition combines functions into a new function that calls them in sequence: the result of one function is passed to the next.
Function composition is one of the fundamental concepts on which category theory is based.

We can also implement function composition recursively. The call pipe(...tail)(head(arg)) is in tail position, but that does not reduce the number of calls. With proper tail calls (ES2015, strict mode only) a tail call does not grow the stack, but among browser engines only JavaScriptCore (Safari) implements them: V8 (Chrome, Node.js) had them behind a flag and removed them, and SpiderMonkey (Firefox) does not have them. That is why deep recursion in JS needs a trampoline — more on it in the "Recursion" lesson. For a pipe of a few functions, stack depth is not a problem.
compose calls the functions right to left, which is fine from a mathematical point of view, while pipe calls them left to right, which is often easier for the reader.
pipe for any number of functions can be written imperatively (with a loop), declaratively (with reduce) or recursively; in real projects, use compose or pipe from existing libraries.

In the lesson, compose is written for exactly three functions, while pipe handles any number of them. Write compose for any number of functions: it should call them right to left. Check that compose(square, double, inc) and pipe(inc, double, square) give the same result, while compose(inc, double, square) gives a different one. Hint: arrays have a reduceRight method — the same as reduce, except that it walks the array from right to left.
